text: The FDA February 28, 2025 roundup reported marketing approval of a software update providing adaptive DBS that adjusts stimulation from detected brain signals. The roundup described use in levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease with symptoms inadequately controlled by medication for at least four years; this historical announcement should not substitute for current device-specific labeling. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-28)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: FDA's PMA database record for Medtronic supplement P960009/S478 (Activa, Percept and SenSight Deep Brain Stimulation Therapy System) lists a decision date of 02/20/2025 and an approval order statement for a new optional programming feature called adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS), within the indication of adjunctive therapy for levodopa-responsive Parkinson's disease of at least 4 years' duration that is not adequately controlled with medication. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: The FDA summary of safety and effectiveness for P960009/S478 states that the aDBS feature has been marketed for Parkinson's disease in Japan with the Percept PC since May 2020 and the Percept RC since November 2022, and in Europe with both models since January 2025. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: The registry record for NCT07398157, a University of California, San Francisco interventional trial titled "Simplified, Scalable, 24-hour Adaptive DBS in Parkinson's Disease", lists overall status RECRUITING (status verified 2026-09), an actual start date of 2026-04-09, an estimated enrollment of 24 and an estimated primary completion date of 2029-11-30; its summary says researchers will compare study-derived adaptive DBS settings with clinically programmed continuous DBS settings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: Oehrn and colleagues reported improved motor symptoms and quality of life versus clinically optimized continuous DBS in a blinded randomized crossover feasibility trial involving four male patients. Their personalized feedback markers were stimulation-entrained gamma oscillations in the subthalamic nucleus or motor cortex; the authors called for larger trials. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: ADAPT-PD enrolled 68 participants previously stable on continuous DBS and medication. Its comparison of adaptive versus continuous DBS was open-label; randomization and blinding compared the two adaptive modes in participants tolerating both. The study therefore does not establish blinded randomized superiority of adaptive over continuous DBS. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: In ADAPT-PD, the post hoc primary performance threshold was met by 91% receiving dual-threshold and 79% receiving single-threshold adaptive DBS. This measured preservation of good on-time relative to continuous DBS rather than a superiority endpoint. Single-threshold treatment reduced total electrical energy delivered by 15%; this was not a measured 15% battery-longevity extension. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: A nine-patient double-blind randomized crossover trial using consecutive one-month treatment periods and beta-band dual-threshold control reported no statistically significant adaptive-versus-continuous DBS differences; the authors reported between-patient heterogeneity and called for adequately powered follow-up. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: In a randomized double-blind crossover assessment of directional versus omnidirectional stimulation, directional stimulation widened the therapeutic window in 183 of 202 evaluable participants (90.6%), with a mean increase of 41%. Therapeutic window denotes stimulation amplitudes achieving symptom relief without side effects; the study enrolled 234 subjects. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: A separate 19-patient randomized directional-versus-omnidirectional crossover trial found no significant differences in primary rigidity or secondary clinical motor outcomes. Its discussion reported 30% lower stimulation intensity with directional stimulation, while chronic motor performance could worsen under the tested directional settings. Wider therapeutic windows should not be equated with universally superior motor outcomes. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: Adaptive DBS adjusts stimulation amplitude using neural feedback; the beta-band dual-threshold approach adjusts amplitude according to subthalamic local-field-potential power. (high confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: The comparative adaptive-DBS literature is heterogeneous: Oehrn and colleagues reported benefit in their four-person personalized gamma-feedback feasibility trial, whereas a nine-person beta-feedback crossover pilot reported no significant treatment differences. These are attributed results from different protocols and populations, not an interchangeable estimate of efficacy. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: Two FDA documents give different dates for the aDBS approval: the PMA database lists a decision date of 02/20/2025 for supplement P960009/S478, while the FDA Roundup of February 28, 2025 says that on Friday, February 21 the FDA approved for marketing a software update to Medtronic's Activa, Percept and SenSight DBS system that adds adaptive deep brain stimulation. The one-day difference is recorded as an attributed discrepancy and is not resolved here. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads

text: The FDA summary of safety and effectiveness for P960009/S478 states that aDBS was not studied in the ADAPT-PD trial with bilaterally implanted neurostimulators, that only subjects with single implanted neurostimulators were eligible, and that the labeling instructs clinicians not to use aDBS with more than one implanted neurostimulator. (low confidence)
keywords: Adaptive closed-loop DBS and directional leads
